A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work. The complete main texts, equations, four tables, and Appendices A–C are readable and support comparison despite extensive reformatting and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports theoretical constructions, proofs, and analytical activation properties. Neither the main text nor the appendices report original empirical outcomes.

after.justification: Section 3.3 reports implementing the constructions in Lemmas 3 and 4 for ReLU and observing their correctness. This is an original qualitative computational outcome, although no numerical results or detailed testing procedure are supplied.

M1.justification: The constructive networks change substantially. v1 uses repeated gradient attenuation after a four-layer representer; v2 introduces duplicated-output indicators and gradient cancellation in Lemmas 8–9. The gradient-selection component also becomes a two-layer construction with a potentially rescaled surviving gradient, requiring corresponding changes in Section 4.2.

E1.justification: v2 adds reported computational coverage of the function-value and gradient constructions through a ReLU implementation check, whereas v1 has no empirical evaluation. No dataset, application benchmark, or tested input population is identified.

E2.justification: Neither version reports empirical comparisons against baseline methods. References to earlier representability theorems are theoretical dependencies, not evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: The added implementation check specifies ReLU and the two constructions in Lemmas 3 and 4 as its evaluation configuration. Neither version supplies test-input selection, numerical precision, sample counts, metrics, or execution budgets for such a check.

E4.justification: Section 3.3 adds a brief computational sanity check of whether the two ReLU constructions behave correctly. No ablation, sensitivity analysis, or distribution-shift study is added.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated runs, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or statistical uncertainty estimates. The new correctness observation introduces none of these practices.

E6.justification: v2 adds the qualitative finding that the ReLU implementations behave correctly. Numerical sufficient-depth claims also decrease from nine to seven layers for the first main theorem and by two layers for the second. These depth claims are theoretical guarantees, not measured performance gains.

T1.justification: Condition 2 replaces three scale parameters with a single eta and different derivative inequalities; the depth formula and central construction lemmas and proofs are substantially revised. Lemma 4 adds the missing requirement that the target gradient vanish when the input gradient is zero. Appendices B–C support the new depth claims, although C.3 retains older bounds in its corollaries.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: simultaneous representation of function values and AD gradients, including prescribed dependence on varying input gradients, for the same activation families. The tighter depth bounds refine these contributions without redefining them.

C2.justification: Section 2.4 adds an explicit explanation of computational-graph dependence in floating-point AD. Section 3.3 discusses extending the results to more general elementwise backward rules. v2 also removes float16 from the examples attached to the E ≥ 6 results, while retaining its coverage through Appendix C.3.

D1.justification: v2 adds a ReLU implementation statement and a code-availability link in Section 3.3, footnote 2; v1 provides neither. The PDFs do not supply execution instructions, test inputs, hardware details, or quantitative validation logs.

R1.justification: The cited works and central positioning relative to earlier function-value representability results remain unchanged. Expanded author names, bibliography relocation, and use of different lemmas from an already cited work do not establish a new research positioning.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and Appendices A–C remain. v2 expands the AD exposition, edits local prose, renames p and q to M and E, changes statement numbering, moves references after the appendices, and removes the generic impact statement.

P2.justification: The two-column conference main text becomes a single-column article with changed typography, spacing, and equation layout. Table 1 replaces its three eta columns with one. The other tables are retained and repositioned; no figures are introduced.

improvement.justification: v2 offers shallower constructions, fuller AD discussion, and a code link, but the revision is incompletely reconciled. Section 4.1 describes the same intermediate network as both one-layer and two-layer; Appendix B.8 retains the old iterative proof alongside its replacement; and C.3 derives depths of seven to nine while its corollaries retain nine-to-thirteen bounds. These inconsistencies obstruct verification of the revised guarantees, preventing a reliable judgment of net quality improvement.
